_doc: Per-file char budgets for instructions/memory files (GHI #373). AGENTS.md was tightened 40k→15k by OBPI-0.0.54-01 as a moderate-compromise target; OBPI-0.0.54-03 measured a ~31k transitional floor with the current monolithic template. The budget ceiling was Codex's 32768-byte project-doc cap until the operator ruling of 2026-07-06 DECOUPLED it (hexagonal: an adapter limit must not gate the core contract); the ceiling is now _PROJECT_DOC_BUDGET_CEILING_BYTES = 65536, enforced by tests.governance.test_agents_md_map_doctrine._budget_within_ceiling. The vendor cap itself is observed, not enforced, by the surface-delivery witness under gz validate --instructions-files-budget (GHI #712) — it reports byte distance to stderr and fail-closes only on survival-declaration drift. 2026-06-04: OBPI-0.0.37-26 LANDED the interim #519 relief — the local splice (.gzkit/agents.local.md) was hand-compressed 9,306→4,997 bytes, dropping rendered root AGENTS.md to 28,342 bytes, under the then-30000 interim ceiling and ~4.4 KB under the Codex byte cap (genuine context reduction, not a budget-at-cap stopgap). This supersedes the transient budget-at-cap reading (32768) that only flipped the gate green without shrinking the surface. The committed rendition (renditions/agentcontract-codex-root-interim.md) is the durable payload OBPI-21/22's composer regenerates deterministically. The <15k destination remains GHI #533 / ADR-0.0.37. 2026-06-22 (operator-ratified): AGENTS.md raised 30000→31000 to seat the corpus-faithful render of the full invariant-tier floor (all 45 entries verbatim render to 30,631 chars / 30,806 bytes). The prior 30000 ceiling could only be met by a rendition that DROPPED invariant entries — i.e. by drift — so the budget was holding the surface honest at the cost of the invariant floor. 31000 matches OBPI-0.0.54-03's measured transitional floor, fits the faithful render with headroom, and stays ~1.9 KB under the 32768 B Codex hard cap (no silent-truncation risk). The <15k destination via corpus splitting remains the durable goal (GHI #533 / ADR-0.0.37). CLAUDE.md 4000 and .claude/rules/*.md 15000 remain from OBPI-0.0.54 AS OF THIS ENTRY (each dated entry states the values true on its own date, never the current ones — read the LAST entry for what is enforced today). 2026-06-30 (operator-directed, budget-tuning explicitly deferred — 'we will use that for tuning later, the mechanism to do so is now in place'): AGENTS.md raised 31000→31800 to seat the corpus-faithful render of 5 new invariant-tier guardrails captured from the 2026-06-30 insights report (pipeline-stage discipline, no --no-verify, narrow-scope discipline, defect/deferred-claim honesty, surface-blockers-upfront). Measured claude/root render = 31,569 bytes (invariant 9,612 / compressible 21,957); 31800 clears it whether counted as chars or bytes and holds ~968 B under the 32768 B Codex hard cap (no silent-truncation risk). This GROWS the surface against the <15k shrink goal (GHI #533 / ADR-0.0.37) — the operator booked that tension as later tuning, not a blocker; the corpus-splitting destination is unchanged. 2026-07-06 (ceiling decoupled BY RULING; the three per-file BUDGETS were raised deliberately, but their rationale went unrecorded until 2026-07-28): the operator ruling 'that hard-coded value is noise, bump' DECOUPLED the ceiling from the Codex vendor cap (32768→65536; hexagonal — an adapter limit must not gate the core contract). In the same commit (219d23fd6, a `gz git-sync` chore bundle) three BUDGETS were raised: AGENTS.md 31800→50000, CLAUDE.md 4000→15000, .claude/rules/*.md 15000→30000. These are NOT drift — see the 2026-07-28 entry, which records the standing pre-1.0 posture they implement. What was genuinely missing was the WRITTEN RATIONALE: `gz git-sync` bundles DERIVED surface regeneration and its commit template carries no slot for 'why did this hand-tuned threshold change', so a deliberate posture arrived on disk looking indistinguishable from drift. That indistinguishability is the defect — not the number. 2026-07-28 (operator ruling, verbatim: 'until we get gzkit stable, I want to relax limits. the cms system is meant to control this, but we don't have gzkit feature stable enough to be strict'): the loose budgets are a DELIBERATE PRE-1.0 RELAXATION, now on the record. Rationale: the corpus/CMS chain (`gz content remember` → `gz content compose` → land) is the intended control surface for per-turn size, and it is not feature-stable — ADR-0.35.0-canon-entry-corpus-landing is Draft at 0/9 OBPIs landed, with the corpus→candidate generator (OBPI-05) and the `gz content land` orchestrator (OBPI-07) both unbuilt. A gate whose satisfaction path does not exist does not force the work; it only blocks it, and then gets widened under pressure — precisely what the 2026-06-30 setting of 231 chars (0.7%) headroom demonstrated by being blown out within a week. Strictness is earned by the mechanism that discharges it. EXIT CONDITION: re-tighten toward the <15k destination (GHI #533 / ADR-0.0.37) when the CMS corpus-splitting path lands — not before. A retune to 33000/4000/19000 was made and REVERTED the same day under this ruling; measurements taken then, recorded for whoever re-tightens: AGENTS.md 32,023 chars / 32,208 B; CLAUDE.md 1,432 chars; largest rule file tests.md 17,851 chars (tests.md already exceeds the pre-2026-07-06 rules budget of 15000, so that value is not restorable without a diet pass on its rule-version-history preamble). Ceiling unchanged at 65536. Reading convention, which is what actually failed here: each dated entry states the values true ON ITS DATE; the LAST entry is what is enforced today. 2026-08-06 (GHI #533 — dead-pointer sweep; BUDGETS UNCHANGED, destination repointed): the EXIT CONDITION above names ADR-0.0.37, which went terminal 2026-07-18 (§ Terminal Disposition, 'Split-and-Supersede') with its registry-spine OBPIs PERMANENTLY WITHDRAWN — no weight-halving work can land there, so that exit condition aimed whoever re-tightens at a destination that cannot accept the work. RESTATED EXIT CONDITION: re-tighten toward the <15k destination when ADR-0.35.0-canon-entry-corpus-landing § Decision 3 lands — sections declare corpus-owned or unowned, the generator materializes owned sections from the corpus, and the unowned byte total is held in a decrease-only ratchet; concretely, when its corpus→candidate generator (OBPI-05) and gz content land orchestrator (OBPI-07) exist. Not before — the 2026-07-28 ruling that strictness is earned by the mechanism that discharges it is unchanged, and repointing the destination does not make the mechanism exist. The four prior mentions of ADR-0.0.37 are left UNMODIFIED on purpose: each sits in a dated entry, that ADR was live on each of those dates, and rewriting them would falsify the record this file's own reading convention depends on. Same-sweep siblings: .gzkit/rules/agents-md-map-doctrine.md (v0.3.0, landed earlier under this GHI) and docs/governance/agents-md-doctrine.md § Budget targets. Superseded planning docs naming ADR-0.0.37 (ultraplan-brief.md, build-to-1.0-campaign-2026-06-10.md, return-to-health-plan-2026-05-30.md) each carry a SUPERSEDED/retained-for-audit banner and are deliberately untouched. 2026-08-17 (operator ruling, verbatim: 'temporary stay of all control surface budget limits until version 1.0. I want to be warned, and we may lift the limits as needed, but no blockers.'): the per-file budgets are now ADVISORY. BUDGET VALUES ARE UNCHANGED — AGENTS.md 50000, CLAUDE.md 15000, .claude/rules/*.md 30000 — and the audit still measures every file and reports each overrun to stderr with its byte distance and the /gz-context-diet pointer; what is suspended is the CONSEQUENCE, never the observation. audit_instructions_files_budget returns no ValidationError and cannot change an exit code. This makes the two arms of `gz validate --instructions-files-budget` consistent: its scope-sibling surface_delivery_witness has been observe-only on the vendor cap since the 2026-07-06 decoupling ruling, so the scope previously fail-closed on the project's own budget while merely warning about the vendor cap that can actually TRUNCATE the surface — strict about the softer limit, advisory about the harder one. The scope still fail-closes through that sibling on survival-declaration drift, and the negative control was repointed there the same day (a control asserting enforcement that no longer happens is worse than no control). Measured at the ruling: AGENTS.md 33153 chars against a 50000 budget, so nothing was blocked by this gate at the time — the stay is a standing posture, not a workaround for a live block. EXIT CONDITION: restore fail-closed at 1.0, on the same 2026-07-28 ground that strictness is earned by the mechanism that discharges it — the corpus/CMS path is what makes an over-budget surface fixable, and ADR-0.35.0 § Decision 3 is where it lands. Reading convention unchanged: this is the LAST entry, so it states what is enforced today. 2026-08-17 (second ruling, same day, verbatim: 'when we exceed vendor limits, ghi it so it doesn't block'): VENDOR-LIMIT EXCEEDANCES ROUTE TO A GHI, NEVER A BLOCK. This is a separate rule from the budget stay above and must not be collapsed into it. The budgets in `files`/`globs` are gzkit's OWN thresholds and are stayed to advisory until 1.0; a vendor delivery cap is a PHYSICAL truncation belonging to the consuming vendor, so no gzkit ruling can stay it and raising a budget cannot relieve it — bytes past the cap are simply not delivered. The surface_delivery_witness has reported vendor-cap distance without blocking since 2026-07-06; what this ruling adds is the TRACKING obligation, so an exceedance lands in a durable record instead of a stderr line that scrolls past. Live record: GHI #815 (AGENTS.md 33153 B against the codex cap 32768 B, 385 B over, with the must-survive section 'architectural-boundaries' straddling the boundary at bytes 32558-33153). The remedies are owned elsewhere and neither is a budget change: ADR-pool.render-order-truncation-survival (reorder must-survive sections ahead of the cap) and GHI #533 (shrink). Note the shape GHI #815 records — must-survive measured 21582 B cumulative against a 32768 B cap under GHI #580, so the declaration is satisfiable and it is the render ORDER that fails. 2026-08-17 (third ruling, same day — TRACKING RECORD MOVED; budgets and both rulings above UNCHANGED): GHI #815 was CLOSED superseded into ADR-pool.render-order-truncation-survival, which now carries the measurement in its Intent and Decision (commit b20b210e4). The entry above names #815 as the 'Live record' — true on its date, and left unmodified per this file's reading convention, but it is no longer where the exceedance is tracked. The vendor-cap exceedance ITSELF IS STILL LIVE: AGENTS.md renders 34354 B against the codex cap 32768 B (1586 B over) and the must-survive section 'architectural-boundaries' begins at byte 33759, wholly past the cap rather than straddling it as it did at 385 B over. Re-measured the same day, the must-survive set (ranks 1-11) totals 23678 B with 9090 B of headroom under the cap, so the declaration is satisfiable with NO shrink and exactly one section falls outside — because it renders LAST. That is why the reorder half (ADR-pool.render-order-truncation-survival) is ranked FIRST as the delivery remedy and GHI #533 (shrink) is ranked second as the cure: a smaller surface in the same order still puts rank 11 last. The tracking obligation from the second ruling is unchanged — if an exceedance has no OPEN GHI, file one via /ghi-author; do not cite #815, resolve first. Note also that #533's own body names ADR-0.0.37 as its blocker, which is STALE: that ADR is Validated 15/15 and the dependency relocated to ADR-0.35.0 Decision 3, Pending at 0/10. 2026-08-17 (fourth ruling, same day — #815 REOPENED and a CORRECTION to the entry above; budgets still UNCHANGED): the operator ruled the cap should carry an open tracker ('I wanted the codex cap to be GHI'd'), so GHI #815 was REOPENED rather than refiled — ghi-author Step 0 reopens a <=30-day close of the same root cause instead of duplicating it into a fresh number. The superseded routing to ADR-pool.render-order-truncation-survival STANDS; the reopen restores a tracker, not a reversal. CORRECTION: the entry above says shrink is 'ranked second as the cure: a smaller surface in the same order still puts rank 11 last.' That is OVERSTATED and the error is material. It holds only while the surface remains OVER the cap; compress AGENTS.md below 32768 B and every section renders inside it, architectural-boundaries included, so shrink IS a delivery fix. The honest axis is durability, not capability: reorder is growth-invariant (must-survive renders first whatever the total) while shrink restores delivery today and decays on the next corpus growth. They are complementary; reorder stays ranked first because its fix does not decay. The prior entry is left UNMODIFIED per this file's reading convention — a dated entry records what was believed on its date, and this correction is itself dated. VEHICLE: the shrink work is chore-shaped, and instructions-files-diet v2.0.0 (GHI #817) is now corpus-aware — it authors against .gzkit/corpus/AGENTS.md.jsonl, composes candidates, and STOPS at the Gate 5 attestation boundary rather than landing canon. v1.0.0 named AGENTS.md as a direct edit target and omitted gz validate --invariant-coherence from its acceptance set, so it could have edited a rendered surface and gone green.
